messages:
Anya (PM): Quick sync: customer asked for a QPS slab product that only applies to a set of high-volume routes. They want predictable monthly spend + overage protection. Need to pick pricing shape and pilot constraints.
Ravi (Sales): They prefer slab pricing (buy N qps up front) because it maps to their budget cycles. But they also want a soft buffer during spikes.
Sophia (Revenue): Two shapes to consider: slab (prepaid reserved qps) vs elastic bucket (credits consumed as traffic flows). Slab gives predictability; bucket gives flexibility. We should table elasticity as premium.
Jin (Eng): Implementation note: slab can be enforced with token-bucket per route + reservation nodes. Bucket requires add'l telemetry for credit burn rate and faster reconciliation. Slab MVP much faster.
Oliver (Legal): Contract notes: if we call it a "slab" must define refill, refunds, early termination. Also specify invoice lines: route name, reserved_qps, period, overage_rate.
Anya (PM): Pilot proposal: 1) Offer a "Route Slab" SKU only (no bucket) for initial pilot; 2) Minimum 3-month commit; 3) soft buffer = 10% burst at no extra charge, then overage at X.
Sophia (Revenue): Agree pilot = slab. Pricing suggestion: $A per 1000 reserved qps/month; overage at 200% of unit price. Migration credit if they reduce commitment inside first billing cycle.
Ravi (Sales): Customer wants per-second granularity in metering to avoid disputes. Can we provide 1s aggregation?
Jin (Eng): We currently emit per-route metrics at 1s in canary tier. We can expose per-route qps utilization and cumulative billable tokens/sec. Need to add reconciliation job for invoice delta. ETA: 2 weeks for visibility + 3 weeks for billing hook.
billing-bot: Note: invoices will include route-level breakdown and a reconciliation tag.
Oliver (Legal): Also require dispute window (30 days) and sample logs attached on dispute request. Need to add clause about how we compute qps (averaging window, rounding).
Anya (PM): UX: Console should let customers map routes to slab product, show expected monthly charge and current utilization gauge. Mock: 
```
Route: /v1/track/clicks
Slab: 50k qps
Utilization: 41k (82%)
Est. monthly charge: $X,XXX
```
Matt (Product): (joining) Suggest we auto-populate recommended slab sizes using 95th pct over last 30d. Option to suggest 25/50/75% above current usage.
Sophia (Revenue): Launch criteria for pilot: 1) 2 partners signed to 3mo trial, 2) route-level metering visible in Console w/ 1s granularity, 3) billing webhook + invoice sample confirmed, 4) legal addendum approved.
Jin (Eng): Risk: capacity fragmentation if many small slabs reserved. Mitigation: pack slabs into shared pools and honor isolation only logically. Could impose minimum slab size (e.g., 1k qps).
Ravi (Sales): Minimum slab size ok, but call it "minimum purchase unit" in sales docs. Customers dislike tiny minimums that inflate costs.
Oliver (Legal): Flag: private deployments may need different pricing and data proof for metering (on-prem HSM logs). Add a paragraph in addendum.
Anya (PM): Action list: Jin = telemetry PR by Tue; Sophia = pricing table v0; Oliver = addendum draft; Ravi = identify 2 pilot customers; PM to run pilot kickoff.
Sophia (Revenue): Also decide on renewal cadence: auto-renew monthly vs block renewals. Recommend auto-renew monthly with option to commit annually for discount.
Jin (Eng): One more infra detail: enforcement semantics on overage. Do we throttle, route to fallback, or just bill? Need to pick default.
Anya (PM): Default = bill overage, do not throttle in pilot. Add option for "hard cap" in contract if customer requests.
Ravi (Sales): Good. I'll pitch slab pilot to the finance customer tomorrow.
Anya (PM): Great, I'll update the product doc and drop a link here when ready. Quick thumbs if you approve pilot scope as slab-only for launch. :thumbsup:
